req.title: Return 405 for unsupported /players root method
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection).

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that DELETE on /players/ (the collection root) must return HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed. The router only registers DELETE on /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}, not on /players/ itself. Tests must: (1) confirm 405 is returned for DELETE /players/ (positive case for the error path), (2) confirm that supported methods on /players/ still work correctly (negative case — GET returns 200, proving the route itself is live), and (3) probe the boundary between the supported DELETE sub-path and the unsupported collection DELETE (boundary case). All assertions use exact status codes to catch constant-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_delete_players_collection_returns_405
preconditions: DELETE /players/ is not registered as a route handler
26 pre-loaded players exist in the database
actions: Send DELETE request to /players/ using TestClient
expected: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed is returned
Status code is exactly 405, not 404 or 200
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_delete_players_collection_returns_405():
    r = client.delete('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 405

expected: Response body is a JSON array with exactly 26 items
trace: R-PLAYER-036: contrasts DELETE (405) with GET (200) on same path to confirm method-level discrimination
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_get_players_collection_returns_200_not_405():
    r = client.get('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 405
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)

actions: Send DELETE request to /players/squadnumber/1 (the supported sub-path)
expected: HTTP 204 No Content is returned for the supported DELETE sub-path
Status code is exactly 204, confirming the boundary between /players/ (405) and /players/squadnumber/{n} (204)
trace: R-PLAYER-036: boundary between unsupported DELETE /players/ (405) and supported DELETE /players/squadnumber/{n} (204)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_delete_players_squadnumber_returns_204_not_405():
    # DELETE on the collection root must be 405
    r_collection = client.delete('/players/')
    assert r_collection.status_code == 405

    # DELETE on the sub-resource path must be 204 (squad number 1 exists)
    r_sub = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert r_sub.status_code == 204
    assert r_sub.status_code != 405

tests.name: test_post_players_collection_returns_201_not_405
preconditions: POST /players/ is a registered route handler
Squad number 99 does not exist in the pre-loaded dataset
actions: Send POST request to /players/ with a valid player body
expected: HTTP 201 Created is returned for POST /players/
Status code is exactly 201, not 405, proving only DELETE is blocked at the collection level
trace: R-PLAYER-036: decision-table row — POST on /players/ is allowed (201), DELETE is not (405)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_post_players_collection_returns_201_not_405():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 99,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post('/players/', json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    assert r.status_code != 405

    # Confirm DELETE on same path still returns 405
    r_del = client.delete('/players/')
    assert r_del.status_code == 405

tests.name: test_delete_players_collection_405_response_headers
preconditions: DELETE /players/ is not a registered route
actions: Inspect status code and Allow header in the response
expected: The Allow header lists the permitted methods (GET, POST) but not DELETE
trace: R-PLAYER-036: verifies exact 405 status and that DELETE is absent from Allow header — catches constant-mutation on status code
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_delete_players_collection_405_response_headers():
    r = client.delete('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    # Allow header must not include DELETE for this path
    allow_header = r.headers.get('allow', '').upper()
    assert 'DELETE' not in allow_header
    # GET and POST should be listed as allowed
    assert 'GET' in allow_header or 'POST' in allow_header
